reason: REFUTED ON THE YEAR ONLY. The quotation itself survives every other attack, so this should be corrected rather than dropped. What holds: I downloaded Gutenberg 3800, the Elwes Ethics, and read the end of Part V locally. The Note to Proposition XLII closes: If the way which I have pointed out as leading to this result seems exceedingly hard, it may nevertheless be discovered. Needs must it be hard, since it is so seldom found. How would it be possible, if salvation were ready to our hand, and could without great labour be found, that it should be by almost all men neglected? But all things excellent are as difficult as they are rare. The proposed line is the last sentence of the Ethics, verbatim, with the opening But that popular quotation usually drops. Translator, work, part and locator are all right, and shipped.js gives no exact or near match, Spinoza at one of three for the year, not banned, in scope, publishable, source line inside 140 characters with no dash. What breaks: the translation year. Elwes' Ethics was not published in 1883. It stands in Volume II of The Chief Works of Benedict de Spinoza, London, George Bell and Sons, and the scanned Volume II on the Internet Archive, in.ernet.dli.2015.47604, is dated 1884; Volume I, in.ernet.dli.2015.47603, is the 1883 one, and library records give the set as 1883 to 1884, Volume I the two political treatises, Volume II the Improvement of the Understanding, the Ethics and the Correspondence. So the card as proposed would print a confident wrong date for the very volume whose wording it uses. The verifier's evidence chain explains how it got there: it rests on the Wikisource text, which names Elwes but states no edition and carries the notice that the work is not backed by a scanned copy of the edition from which it was transcribed, so 1883 was never read off any title page. Fix the year to 1884, or, if the editor would rather not pin a volume he has not seen, name the translator alone.
